name: TitleCapture
description: Each US title company gets its own white-label app. Its real-estate agents and lenders use it to make title quotes, seller net sheets, and buyer estimates without calling a title rep. Miami. Started October 2013.

mentions.evidence: Self-reported, Starter Story, 20 November 2023. Not independently checked. "$300K+ MRR (close to $4m ARR)". The page header says $333K of revenue a month, 2 founders, and 35 employees. More than 1,500 title companies, "close to 10% of the entire title company market." Around 30% profitability, and they have never taken funding. About $300 a month per title company.
mentions.indieAngle: A back-office industry where the customer gives your tool to its own customers.

whyItPrints: A title company hands "their app" to its agents. The founder says churn is very low, because taking the app back is hard. The fee is about $300 a month. One industry partnership took them from 1 customer to more than 150 in the first year.
whyThisMatters:
A title company in the US gets an app with its own name on it. Agents and lenders use that app for a title quote, a seller's net sheet, and a buyer's estimate. They do not have to call a rep for the arithmetic. The company is in Miami, and it started in October 2013.

The interview is from November 2023. I am not treating it as this week's number. The story says more than three hundred thousand a month, close to four million a year. The page header is a bit higher than that phrase, with two founders and thirty-five people. More than fifteen hundred title companies, which the founder calls close to a tenth of that market. About thirty percent profit, and no funding. The fee is about three hundred a month per company.

The lock-in is the handoff. Once the agents have "their" app, taking it away is awkward. The first year went from one customer to more than a hundred and fifty through one industry partnership. You pay so the quote happens in the company's own app.
